subtitle: How grants, samantas, and merchants fed the temples of Jejakabhukti

panels.shot: dramatic three-quarter view, low-angle, of Satyabhama holding up a gleaming copper plate against a backdrop of Khajuraho temples and distant forts
panels.action: Satyabhama stands in the foreground, one hand lifting a freshly inscribed copper plate as temple shikharas of Khajuraho rise behind her and, in the far haze, the rocky silhouette of Kalinjar and village fields stretch to the horizon.

dialogue.text: Beneath the stone of Khajuraho, copper plates, village fields and samantas quietly fed the Chandela realm.

i18n.hi: खजुराहो की चट्टानों के नीचे, ताम्रपत्र, खेत और सामंत चुपचाप चंदेला राज्य को खिलाते रहे।

panels.shot: slow push-in on a copper plate being unearthed in a modern village field, time-blend hinting at past and present
panels.action: A farmer’s hand brushes away soil from a buried copper plate in a central Indian field, while above the same ground we faintly see an older scene of scribes and officials gathered around a fresh grant.

dialogue.text: From Kundeshwar to Nanyaura, buried copper plates whisper how the Chandela kings ruled through land, water and promise.

i18n.hi: कुंडेश्वर से नन्यौरा तक, गड़े ताम्रपत्र फुसफुसाते हैं कि चंदेला राजाओं ने ज़मीन, पानी और वादों से राज किया।

panels.shot: medium shot of Satyabhama seated in a modest yet dignified household, with scribes nearby, scrolls and copper plates laid out
panels.action: Satyabhama sits cross-legged in a torchlit hall, calm and focused, as a royal scribe etches characters onto a glowing strip of copper while assistants arrange older plates and palm-leaf records beside her.

dialogue.text: Around 1004, Satyabhama’s grant at Kundeshwar fixed a Chandela king’s date, but it also fixed a village’s fate.

i18n.hi: लगभग १००४ में, कुंडेश्वर की सत्यभामा-दत्ता ने चंदेला राजा की तारीख भी ठोकी, और गांव की किस्मत भी।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder close-up of the copper plate surface as letters are incised, with a faint reflection of Satyabhama’s face
panels.action: The stylus of the scribe presses into soft copper, forming crisp Nagari letters, while Satyabhama’s attentive face appears reflected on the polished metal surface.

dialogue.text: The inscription names gifts of land and rights, a precise place, a purpose, a king, a donor, and the witnesses who will remember.

i18n.hi: शिलालेख में ज़मीन और हक़ के दान, ठिकाना, मकसद, राजा, दाता और गवाह सब दर्ज हैं।

panels.shot: wide rural landscape shot showing a village, tanks, fields and a distant temple under construction
panels.action: A broad view of Jejakabhukti shows farmers in terraced fields, a large irrigation tank glinting in the sun, bullock carts creaking along a mud path, and the skeleton of a stone temple rising in the distance.

dialogue.text: The plates speak of land and villages, not cities alone: of fields, tanks, groves and the people bound to serve them.

i18n.hi: ये पट्टे शहर नहीं, गांवों की बात करते हैं: खेत, ताल, उपवन और उन्हें सेवा में जोड़े लोग।

panels.shot: medium shot of a samanta chieftain at the Dubkund region, presenting himself at court with folded hands
panels.action: A Kachchhapaghata chief, Arjuna, stands respectfully before a Chandela throne, hands folded, a sword at his waist, as attendants and scribes watch in a polished audience hall.

dialogue.text: In Dubkund, Arjuna of the Kachchhapaghatas left stone words that he served the Chandela king Vidyadhara as samanta, a feudatory yet a lord in his own land.

i18n.hi: डुबकुंड में कच्छपघाट अरजुन ने पत्थर पर लिखा कि वह चंदेला राजा विद्याधर का सामंत था—जागीरदार, पर अपनी धरती का मालिक।

panels.shot: split-scene composition: left side showing Arjuna leading troops, right side showing him presiding over local justice and land
panels.action: On one side, Arjuna rides at the head of mailed horsemen near a rocky fort; on the other, he sits beneath a banyan tree hearing villagers’ disputes as a land surveyor marks boundary stones.

dialogue.text: As samanta, Arjuna owed military service and loyalty; in return he held land, collected dues and carved his own name into the stone of Dubkund.

i18n.hi: सामंत के नाते अरजुन पर फौजी सेवा और निष्ठा का कर्ज था; बदले में ज़मीन, लगान और डुबकुंड की चट्टान पर अपना नाम मिला।

panels.shot: medium temple-entrance shot of merchants at Kalinjar’s Chandi Darwaza, with their inscription panel in view
panels.action: A group of cloth-wrapped merchants stands near the arched gateway of Kalinjar, hands raised in reverence to an unseen deity, as a stone slab on the wall bears a freshly carved donor inscription.

dialogue.text: At Kalinjar’s Chandi Darwaza, early merchant inscriptions record gifts, routes and names, tying distant traders to this hill of gods and kings.

i18n.hi: कालींजर के चंडी दरवाज़े पर पुराने व्यापारी-लेख दान, रास्ते और नाम दर्ज करते हैं, दूर-दराज़ के सौदागरों को इस देव-राजा की पहाड़ी से जोड़ते हैं।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of the Kalinjar gateway with caravans passing underneath, pilgrims and soldiers mingling
panels.action: Long caravans of pack-animals and ox-carts pass beneath the massive gateway of Kalinjar, brushing past armed guards and saffron-clad pilgrims climbing toward the fortress-temple above.

dialogue.text: The fort became a node: merchants sought protection and prestige, kings sought taxes and honour, temples sought steady offerings.

i18n.hi: किला एक गाँठ बन गया: व्यापारी सुरक्षा और मान के लिए आए, राजा कर और यश के लिए, मंदिर लगातार चढ़ावे के लिए।

panels.shot: intimate interior shot of a temple accountant counting coins and weighing grain in a Khajuraho shrine store-room
panels.action: Inside a Khajuraho temple store-room, a grey-bearded accountant squats beside jars of grain and stacks of coins, using a balance scale as young assistants tally donations on palm leaves.

dialogue.text: Temple endowments were not stone alone; inscriptions describe fields, oil-presses, markets and shares of produce feeding the lamps and the priests.

i18n.hi: मंदिरों को बस पत्थर नहीं मिला; शिलालेखों में खेत, तेलघट, हाट-बाज़ार और उपज के हिस्से दिए, जो दीपों और पुजारियों को खिलाते थे।

panels.shot: wide shot of a water tank near Khajuraho with pilgrims and vendors around its steps
panels.action: A broad stone tank near Khajuraho reflects the sky as pilgrims bathe at its ghats, while vendors sell food and garlands under palm-leaf shelters and a small shrine guards the water’s edge.

dialogue.text: Water, too, became wealth: tanks endowed by grants drew pilgrims, who in turn drew traders and craftsmen, weaving a small economy around each sacred shore.

i18n.hi: पानी भी दौलत बना: दान से बने तालाब तीर्थियों को खींचते, तीर्थी बदले में व्यापारी और कारीगर लाते, हर घाट पर छोटी अर्थव्यवस्था बुनते।

panels.shot: close-up of Madanavarman-era coins being poured from a cloth bag into a merchant’s hand
panels.action: A merchant’s calloused palm receives a spill of small, shining coins from a cloth pouch, their Chandela emblems clearly visible as they clink into his hand in a busy marketplace.

dialogue.text: Under Madanavarman, coins appear in abundance, a late sign that the Chandela realm still pulsed with trade and payments when stone building slowed.

i18n.hi: मादनवर्मन के समय सिक्के भरभराकर मिलते हैं—यह देर का निशान है कि पत्थर-निर्माण सुस्त पड़ा, पर चंदेला राज्य में लेन-देन धड़कते रहे।

panels.shot: medium shot of Satyabhama handing the Kundeshwar copper plate to assembled brahmana donees and village elders
panels.action: Satyabhama stands before a small assembly near Kundeshwar, solemnly passing the inscribed copper plate into the hands of seated brahmanas as village elders watch with mixed curiosity and hope.

dialogue.text: Guard this grant, and the land will guard you.

i18n.hi: इस दान को संभालो, ज़मीन तुम्हारी रखवाली करेगी।

panels.shot: close-up on the gathered faces of villagers reacting as the grant is proclaimed aloud by a scribe
panels.action: A royal scribe reads aloud from the plate, while villagers—farmers, a potter, a weaver—listen intently, some relieved, some wary, as the new rights and obligations settle over their lives.

dialogue.text: Such grants conferred tax exemptions and duties, shifting who paid whom and who could claim the sweat of these fields.

i18n.hi: ऐसे दानों ने कर-छूट और नई जिम्मेदारियाँ दीं, तय किया कौन किसे देगा और इन खेतों के पसीने पर किसका हक़ होगा।

panels.shot: scholarly montage: modern historians comparing inscriptions, maps and coins on a table, with Chandela sites faint in the background
panels.action: In a present-day study, historians lean over a table strewn with estampages of inscriptions, maps of central India, and trays of coins, while ghostly outlines of Khajuraho and Kalinjar appear beyond the window.

dialogue.text: Modern scholars, from B.D. Chattopadhyay to Cynthia Talbot, piece together this economy from scattered plates, stones and coins, not from a neat archive.

i18n.hi: आज के विद्वान, बी.डी. चट्टोपाध्याय से सिंथिया टैल्बॉट तक, साफ़ रजिस्टर नहीं, बिखरे ताम्रपत्र, पत्थर और सिक्कों से यह अर्थव्यवस्था जोड़ते हैं।

panels.shot: reflective wide shot at dusk of Khajuraho’s temples above darkening fields and a village, Satyabhama’s silhouette faint in the foreground
panels.action: As dusk falls, Khajuraho’s carved towers glow faintly above darkening fields and a small village; in the foreground, the faint silhouette of Satyabhama holds a copper plate against the last light.

dialogue.text: The Chandela order was not a copy of distant feudal worlds, but its own web of samantas, grants and markets, where copper plates quietly held up towers of stone.

i18n.hi: चंदेला व्यवस्था किसी दूर की सामंती नकल नहीं, अपनी सी जाल थी—सामंतों, दानों और बाज़ारों की, जहाँ ताम्रपत्रों ने चुपचाप पत्थर के शिखर संभाल रखे थे।

title_i18n.en: Copper Plates Feed the Chandela Realm
title_i18n.hi: ताम्रपत्रों ने चंदेला राज्य को पोस दिया

subtitle_i18n.en: How grants, samantas, and merchants fed the temples of Jejakabhukti
subtitle_i18n.hi: दान, सामंत और व्यापारी कैसे जे젝भुक्ति के मंदिरों को चलाते थे
